reviewFindings.summary: Slack identity revocation is not wired to required lifecycle producers.
reviewFindings.details: S10-T01 requires organization-scoped Slack identity bindings to revoke when a user requests unlinking, when organization membership or the user is suspended, and when the Slack connection is replaced. The implementation registers internal revoker functions for user_suspended, membership_suspended, and connection_replaced, and tests call those functions directly. However, the task-owned membership, user, and provider-connection lifecycle producer paths do not invoke these revokers; connection replacement is additionally handled opportunistically only when a later consume observes a stale generation. Active bindings can therefore remain durable after the required lifecycle producers fire.
evidence: rtk rg -n "revokeSlackIdentityLinksFor|user_suspended|membership_suspended|connection_replaced" packages/convex/confect packages/convex/test docs/product/maestro-brain-lifecycle-adoption/S10-T01.md shows no caller in membership/user/connection lifecycle producers.

knownRisks: Task-owned lifecycle producer adapters are registered in the Slack identity contract; upstream producer call sites outside the S10-T01 file locks remain integration wiring work if required by a later owner.
